key_insight: The paper turns aggregation-diffusion PDE solving into a variational neural transport problem, using a neural network to learn the velocity field that drives density evolution under Onsager's principle.
engineering_relevance: This offers a scalable simulation strategy for nonlinear transport in materials and soft-matter systems where chemotaxis-, polymer-, and interaction-driven dynamics are expensive to solve directly.
method: Formulate the PDE as a constrained optimal control problem with velocity as the control.
Evolve density with a continuity equation and train the velocity network on a variational objective along particle trajectories.
Couple density and generalized score equations with Euler time stepping for efficient loss evaluation and analysis.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical experiments on several representative models and a rigorous error analysis covering approximation, optimization, Monte Carlo sampling, and time-discretization errors.
watch_item: Performance may depend on trajectory sampling, time-step stability, and the quality of score propagation, which can affect training cost and accuracy.
paper_title: Variational neural transport for aggregation-diffusion equations
